queue.claim: In measured adults, the eye line sits at about 0.48–0.53 of vertex–menton height (brow 0.42–0.46, subnasale 0.69–0.73, stomion 0.78–0.82). These are the default block-in and canon values in Table 2 / loomis_vertical_canon_normalized.
queue.query: Farkas total head height v-gn mean adult male female mm nasion vertex anthropometry

queue.claim: In Loomis's ideal adult head the height is 3.5 units: crown to hairline 1/2 unit, then three equal units (hairline to brow, brow to nose base, nose base to chin). This puts the eye line exactly at half height.
queue.query: Loomis Drawing the Head and Hands head three and one half units hairline brow nose chin proportions

queue.claim: Mouth width (ch–ch) is narrower than the interpupillary distance in adults, at about 0.78–0.88 of it. Nose width over intercanthal width (al–al/en–en) is about 1.0–1.12 in Europeans and higher in African and East Asian samples. Suggested sigmas are 0.07–0.12.
queue.query: mouth width interpupillary distance ratio adults anthropometry cheilion alar width intercanthal ratio

queue.claim: Ear length (sa–sba) is usually longer than nasal height (n–sn), at about 1.10–1.25×, so the canon that the ear spans brow to nose base rarely holds. The profile is roughly square, at about 0.9–1.0.
